newsitem.title: FRANCE: French wheat slips on poor export prospects.
newsitem.headline: French wheat slips on poor export prospects.

text.p: French wheat prices slipped on Tuesday on slack export prospects, dealers said.
Wheat into Rouen was quoted at 850 francs per tonne for December delivery and at 840 francs for January, both down five francs on Monday.

Exporters said the latest sale of Argentine and Australian wheat to Egypt suggested French wheat continued to suffer from competition in its traditional markets from cheaper supplies from other large grain producers.
Algeria is working on a tender to buy 150,000 tonnes of French, U.S. or Argentine milling wheat for shipment in January and February.
But exporters doubted French wheat stood a chance against cheaper Argentine suplies.
One banking source, however, said Algeria still had credit outstanding to buy over 200,000 tonnes of French wheat under an existing Coface credit line that will expire at the end of the year.
Wheat futures volume on MATIF was a thin 35 lots, with the February 1997 expiry quoted at 871 francs per tonne, unchanged from Monday.
